This package provides functions to perform determine sample size for
linear mixed models based on precision.

## Basic installation

Basic installation can be done via the `install_github()` function from
the `remotes` package.

``` r

#install the package
remotes::install_github("Kneerav/precisionSim")
```

Once installed, you can load the library and use the various functions.

``` r

library(precisionSim)
```

## Basic usage

``` r

library(lme4)
library(precisionSim)

#create model
mod1 <- lmer(peak_force ~ task + (1|participant), data=fake_data)

#define function that extracts the interval of interest
interval_function <- function(fitted_model){

  #fit emmeans
  em_df <- emmeans::emmeans(fitted_model, pairwise ~ task)

  #get ci
  ci <- as.data.frame(
    confint(
      em_df$contrasts, level = 0.95, adjust="none"
    )
  )

  #return object
  return(
    data.frame(
      estimand = ci$contrast,
      estimate = ci$estimate,
      lower = ci$lower.CL,
      upper = ci$upper.CL
    )
  )
}

#run precision sim
sim1 <- precisionSim(
  fit = mod1,
  target_width = c(0.1, 0.2),
  interval_fun = interval_function,
  prob = 0.80,
  mc_conf_level = 0.95,
  nsim = 100,
  seed = 123456,
  singular_action = "include",
  nonconverged_action = "exclude",
  tol = 1e-4
)

#check
summary(sim1)

#plot
plot(sim1, type="assurance")

#plot
plot(sim1, type="distribution")

#recheck quantiles
quantile(sim1, prob = c(0.5, 0.8))
```

## Documentation

Full documentation and vignettes are hosted here:
<https://kneerav.github.io/precisionSim/index.html>

## Related work

The package uses model-fitting and simulation functionality provided by
lme4 and design-extension functionality provided by simr.

This work was inspired by the simr package, which uses simulated to
determine statistical power for mixed models. To expand on this
framework (based around significance testing), this package uses
simulation to determine confidence interval widths for a user-supplied
estimand of interest from a linear mixed model from the lme4 package.
This estimand may be a model coefficient, a marginal mean, or a pairwise
contrast of interest.

Similar to the simr package, functions are provided to determine the
assurance probability for a pre-specified confidence interval width, or
to generate a series of assurance probabilities at different simulated
sample sizes (using simr::extend()).

architecture, S3 conventions, validation, testing, and documentation.
